note: TEI patches for 8999 (Glossa ordinaria in Evangelium secundum Joannem, PL 114, cols 0355B-0426B). Read against archive.org patrologiaecursu0114mign -- the SECOND WITNESS established for this volume on 9001: colour, 2215x3603, clean at both margins where our on-disk PL 114 scan clips them. Leaf n = (column + 11) / 2, calibrated on THIS work's own range from the printed corner numbers before any read (n183 = 355/356) and re-read on every leaf used.
class: CORRUPTED = CC broke or lost what Migne set correctly; repaired here, and no [sic:] may stand against Migne on any of them. NORMALIZED = CC silently TIDIED a defect Migne actually printed; Migne's reading is RESTORED and a [sic:] is OWED but deliberately not fired, because firing one is a fresh public claim per site. ⛔ The reader who found the last two normalizations argued against restoring them on the ground that it 'would introduce two non-words'. That is precisely the reasoning this convention overrides, and 9001 settled it: it restored Tlbi (a wrong dotless-l sort) and cruxifixum. Our Latin is not a corrected Latin, it is Migne's page.
result: PLATE READ COMPLETE 2026-09-03, BEFORE the work shipped. Six readers, 18 leaves (n184-n192, n196-n200, n203-n205, n210-n217), all 23 [var:] and all 3 [cj:] read, plus 19 oddities the stints logged unmarked. ⭐ 23 of 23 [var:] CONFIRMED as Migne's, ZERO withdrawn -- with 9004 (46/46) and 9001 (19/19) that is 88 of 88 across three Glossa books. Zero [sic:] were fired by any stint, so nothing could fall. The 17 patches below all come from the SECONDARY pass over declined oddities and from lines read in passing; not one comes from a fired marker.

patches.find: unum sicut et <LACUNA> haec est pax illa
patches.replace: unum sicut et nos, haec est pax illa
patches.why: Leaf n213 of archive.org patrologiaecursu0114mign (cols 415/416), RIGHT column, band D, last line of the column, verified at the plate: 'Gaudium quod supra expressit, ut sint unum sicut et nos, haec est pax illa et beatitudo in | [0417A] futuro saeculo'. ⭐ MIGNE HAS NO LACUNA HERE. CC lost exactly one word -- nos -- at a column break and then tagged the REST OF THE PARAGRAPH <LACUNA>, through 'dicit in mundo', all of which the plate prints continuously and identically (the 0417A remainder re-checked on leaf n214). ⛔ The tag is worse than a visible hole because chunk-work strips it and KEEPS the text, so the chunk would have read 'ut sint unum sicut et haec est pax illa' -- a broken clause with nothing to say it was broken, and a stint would have translated it as continuous prose or fired a marker against Migne for a defect that is ours. Patched at chunking rather than left for the stint. No [ed:] and no [sic:] is owed at this site.

patches.find: quam se esse locutum dicit in mundo.</LACUNA>
patches.replace: quam se esse locutum dicit in mundo.
patches.why: The orphaned CLOSING tag of the same spurious <LACUNA>, at the end of the paragraph on leaf n214 (cols 417/418), left column, band A. Removed with its opener so no unmatched tag survives to make a later chunk run report a lacuna in this work that the plate does not print. Text unchanged; the tag was stripped harmlessly either way.

patches.find:
redemptum, nam sciebat
<pb n="0361A"/>
bat eum Filium Dei esse
patches.replace:
redemptum, nam sciebat
<pb n="0361A"/>
eum Filium Dei esse
patches.why: Leaf n186 (cols 361/362). Migne breaks ONE word across the column break: the foot of col. 360 reads 'nam scie-' with a hyphen, and col. 361 opens 'bat eum Filium Dei esse'. CC resolved the hyphenation to 'sciebat' AND kept the orphan syllable 'bat' as well, so our file printed the syllable twice. The orphan is deleted and the <pb> anchor left between whitespace rather than set mid-word, so the chunker's column-continuity validation is unaffected. English needs no change: 'bat' was never rendered as a word. ⚑ FIRST OF FIVE INSTANCES OF THE HYPHEN-REJOIN CLASS IN THIS WORK.
Leaf n192, col. 373 band D. Migne prints a comma; CC set a full stop. The English carried the stop through under Pattern 8, which is no longer warranted.

Leaf n192, col. 373 band D. Migne prints 'qui potest credere et ideo credere :' -- the second credere with its full -re termination, in the same roman type and size as the first four words earlier on the SAME LINE, which makes the comparison direct rather than inferential. CC dropped the -re and turned his infinitive into an imperative.

Leaf n192, col. 373 band D. Migne sets the siglum '(Isa.)' with NO numeral; our note carries 'VII'. ⚑ Unlike the other patches this is an ADDITION of a correct chapter number, not an OCR shape -- an editorial supplement somewhere upstream. Patched because CLAUDE.md rule 9 keeps fontes RAW VERBATIM and derives the controlled vocabulary later FROM the accumulated raws: a silently supplied numeral corrupts that pool with a precision Migne did not print. ⛔ Checked before patching that no following Ibid. depends on this reference (runbook false-positive 2).

Leaf n205, col. 399 band B. Migne prints the word hyphenated at the line turn, 'im-' / 'pleretur'. CC rejoined it across the break and misread the l. HYPHEN-REJOIN CLASS. English: the stint's Pattern 7 carry-plus-bracketed-sense device ('might impieretur [be fulfilled]') was built only because attribution was unavailable, and is unwound to plain 'might be fulfilled'.
Leaf n205, col. 400 band C. Plate reads 'Sed' with a clean d ascender; CC misread d as a. English: 'Sea for the people' becomes 'But for the people'.

Leaf n210, col. 410 band D. Migne prints 'li-' / 'gnis' across a line break = lignis, 'woods'. CC misread the second half. HYPHEN-REJOIN CLASS. English: the italic Pattern 7 carry of 'liguis' goes and the word is translated, which also restores the Latin-vs-English span parity cruces-0020 flagged.

Leaf n211, col. 411 band C. Migne prints 'Haec mando' in italic, set whole on one line, no break and no damage -- the lemma of Jo 15:17. CC misread d as a. ⚑ Explicitly NOT the 9001 @0203A magnitudino case: there the plate itself carried the non-word, here the plate is clean.

Leaf n213, col. 415 band A. Migne prints 'inter-' / 'rogare' across a line break -- the plain complementary infinitive with volebant. CC misread r as t in the second half. HYPHEN-REJOIN CLASS. ⚑ The reader noted that the same column prints interroges, interrogeris, interrogavit and interrogatus correctly, AND explicitly refused to rest the verdict on that, because corroboration proves an error exists and never whose it is. The ground is the printed 'inter-' / 'rogare'.

Leaf n210, col. 410 band D. Migne prints a comma, magnified and unambiguous; CC set a mid-sentence full stop. ⚑ cruces-0020 lists this stop among the punctuation it FAITHFULLY CARRIED from the plate -- it is not on the plate, and that is the shape of the trap: a stint can only be faithful to the file it is given.

patches.find: <hi>ut omne quod dedisti ei det eis vitam aeternam:</hi>
patches.replace: <hi>ut omne quod ei dedisti ei det eis vitam aeternam:</hi>
patches.why: Leaf n213, col. 416 band A. Migne's italic lemma prints 'ei' TWICE ('ut omne quod ei dedisti ei det eis'), read at 4x; CC dropped the first. A lost word, not a broken one.

Leaf n188, col. 365 band B, verified at 5x: Migne prints 'Funiculis peccatorum suorum quisque CONTRINGITUR (Prov. v.)' -- a genuine non-word. CC silently normalised it to the real word constringitur. ⭐ THE CLASS NO VULGATE COLLATION CAN EVER REACH, because the digitization removed the evidence before any collation ran -- the mirror of 9003's manufactured judicabit->judicavit. Migne's reading restored; a [sic:] is owed here and deliberately not fired. ⚑ The existing 0365B [var:] text and its crux both quote the normalised form and are corrected to match.
Leaf n210, col. 410 band D, read at 4x: Migne prints 'sed quod habet CUPIDITES et infirmitas carnis.' -- a non-word for cupiditas. CC tidied it. Migne's reading restored, [sic:] owed and not fired.

Leaf n212, col. 414 band D, read at 4x: Migne prints 'REDIT SD PATRIAM, quia amatoribus suis se aequalem credendum docuit Patri.' -- 'sd' for ad, a damaged or foul sort. CC tidied it to ad. Migne's reading restored, [sic:] owed and not fired.

Leaf n215, col. 420 band C, read at 3x: Migne prints 'pro qua mortalis FIERIT voluit' -- a non-word. CC tidied it to fieri. Migne's reading restored, [sic:] owed and not fired. ⚑ Found while confirming the Jo 1:29 [var:] two lines above, not by hunting.

Leaf n214, col. 417 band B: Migne prints 'sanctificati IU veritate' -- iu for in, a turned or wrong sort. CC tidied it. Migne's reading restored, [sic:] owed and not fired. ⛔ The reader proposed NO patch for this and the preceding one, reasoning that restoring them 'would introduce two non-words'. That is the reasoning the NORMALIZED convention exists to override, and 9001 settled it by restoring Tlbi and cruxifixum. Recorded here so the disagreement is visible rather than silently resolved.

Leaf n191 (cols 371/372), RIGHT column, band D, read 2026-09-03 AT THE MERGE after blind reader 1 raised it -- col. 372 was in no plate-reader's assigned set, so this leaf was fetched and calibrated for it (printed corners read 371/372). Migne prints 'sed utebatur QUODAM non legitimo'; CC misread a as u. The following 'de quo' already proves the referent is a person, and the English had been carrying the non-word untranslated in italics under Pattern 7, which handed the reader a nonsense noun where a man should stand. English now reads 'a certain man not lawful'. THE SAME READ SETTLED A SECOND THING, IN THE OTHER DIRECTION: Migne really does print the MASCULINE 'qui nondum vocaverat virum' of the woman, so our English's 'she who' is a silent supply of the feminine. Left standing -- the sense is not in doubt -- but recorded in cruces rather than left invisible, because it is the same operation that, run the other way, produces the mechanism-5 defects this read was hunting.
